When Spain began Texas missions
column2: In 1690 Spain began establishing missions among Texas Indians as a buffer against the French.

column1: When Spain first explored and then colonized California
column2: Spaniards first explored California's coast in 1542, but the Crown authorized permanent colonization only in 1768.

column1: How many French lived along the St. Lawrence by 1760
column2: By 1760 about 75,000 French colonists, soldiers and priests lived in the St. Lawrence valley, mostly through natural increase.

column1: When Louisiana was founded
column2: In 1698 Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville founded French Louisiana with a post at Biloxi Bay.

column1: When the Company of the Indies brought slaves to Louisiana
column2: In 1719 the Company of the Indies brought nearly 6,000 slaves, overwhelmingly men, directly from Africa to Louisiana.

column1: When the Natchez rose against the French
column2: In 1729 the Natchez, joined by some newly arrived slaves, rose against the French and killed or captured about 500 colonists.

column1: When King William's War and Queen Anne's War were fought
column2: King William's War was fought from 1689 to 1697 and Queen Anne's War from 1702 to 1713, followed by about 25 years of Anglo-French "cold war" over trade.

column1: How many British and French colonists there were in 1720
column2: In 1720 Britain had nearly 400,000 colonial subjects and France only about 25,000, yet France's Indian alliances blocked British expansion west of the Appalachians.

column1: How many Scots-Irish, Germans and Africans came in the 1700s
column2: In the 1700s about 250,000 Africans in chains, about 250,000 Scots-Irish and about 135,000 Germans came to the British colonies.

column1: How high the colonial birthrate was
column2: The colonial birthrate was triple today's, with most women bearing five to eight children and most children surviving to adulthood.

column1: How many Americans were of African ancestry in 1775
column2: By 1775 one in five Americans was of African ancestry, and over 90 percent of black Americans lived in the South.

column1: When slave imports to the South peaked
column2: The four decades after 1700 were the heaviest years of slave importation to the Chesapeake and Carolina.

column1: When the Stono Rebellion occurred
column2: In 1739 nearly 100 Africans led by Jemmy rose in South Carolina's Stono Rebellion, the largest slave revolt of the colonial period.

column1: When the Great Awakening began
column2: The Great Awakening first appeared in the 1730s among Presbyterians and Congregationalists in the middle colonies and New England.

column1: When Whitefield toured the colonies
column2: George Whitefield arrived in fall 1739 and preached from Georgia to New Hampshire for two years, sailing home in 1741.

column1: When Presbyterian and Baptist churches spread south
column2: From the mid-1740s to the 1770s scores of new Presbyterian and Baptist churches formed in the South and backcountry.

column1: How big the middle class was in England and America
column2: Less than one-third of the English were middle class, compared with nearly three-quarters of white colonists.
